findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return a Result type and use map_err to convert io::Error into a domain error (e.g. LoadError::Io)

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the value field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g. 'foo,abc') panics the caller instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a typed error taxonomy

findings.problem: lossy as cast from u32 to u16: large parse values silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 parses as u32 successfully then truncates to 44464 via u16::MAX+1 wrap, producing data corruption without any error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing on a Vec produced by split
findings.failure_mode: a line with no commas produces a single-element Vec; parts[1] on line 19 will panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Malformed) to get name and value_str safely

findings.problem: println!() is a hidden I/O side effect mixed into data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: the loading function has observable side effects that make it non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and violate pure-core / imperative-shell separation
findings.fix: remove println!; if logging is needed, return a loaded-name enum variant or separate the I/O logging into the shell layer that calls the pure parser

findings.problem: load_packets combines file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), and parsing in a single function
findings.failure_mode: no separation of concerns prevents testing the parsing logic without a real file, and the function cannot be composed into a pure pipeline
findings.fix: split into shell function load_packets(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file and delegates to a pure core function parse_records(&[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: Record uses raw pub String and pub u16 fields with no type-level invariants
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct a Record with an empty name, negative value (not possible for u16, but the type gives no domain meaning), or otherwise invalid state without any constructor gate
findings.fix: add a fallible constructor Record::new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> that validates invariants (non-empty name, valid range), or use newtypes like RecordName(String) with a smart constructor

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> allocates intermediate heap for every line when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation per line; for high-throughput packet loading this adds measurable GC pressure and cache misses
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and borrow &str slices instead of collecting into Vec<String>; trim only the value field and parse directly

findings.problem: no domain error type is defined; the function returns Vec<Record> with no error channel
findings.failure_mode: all failures are expressed through panic, making error recovery impossible and hiding the full set of failure modes from the caller
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Invalid(usize, String), Overflow(usize) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: raw primitives (String, u32) enter the domain through the function signature without a parse-boundary smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: callers can bypass validation and construct invalid Record states directly
findings.fix: parse at the boundary into newtypes via fallible constructors; load_packets should be the shell entry point that validates all external data

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure load_packets throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf record) for allocation hotspots
no allocation analysis (e.g. dhat-rs, --printAllocationStats) for Vec<String> per-line overhead
no command evidence: no cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy run
no second-ring evidence: no Kani, Miri, or property tests for truncation behavior
no CLI command harness or integration test demonstrating load_packets end-to-end
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKERs remain: unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, and hidden I/O in parsing logic. The function must be refactored into a pure parser core with a typed error taxonomy before this crate can be considered compliant. No commands were executed in this static-only review.
